docs.title: VQL (Valthera Query Language)
docs.text: VQL is a query framework for ValtheraDB. It provides two query syntaxes, cross-database relation loading, an optional path-based permission system, an HTTP endpoint, and adapters for non-Valthera data sources.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Dual syntax: VQLS strings for scripts and CLI, VQLR objects for application code and TypeScript.
  • Multiple databases: one processor can serve any number of named ValtheraDB instances.
  • Relations: joins across collections and databases, including nested relations and many-to-many through pivot collections.
  • Variables: predefined _me, _user, _now, _nowShort, __now, and __nowShort, plus custom values.
  • Permissions: optional CRUD and field-level checks with result filtering, backed by your own function or Gate Warden.
  • Adapters: run VQL over an HTTP API, a custom SDK, or per-collection handlers.
  • HTTP API: ready-made Falcon Frame integration with structured errors.
  • Browser compatible: the parser, validator, permissions, and adapters run in the browser when the database is remote.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
bun add @wxn0brp/vql @wxn0brp/db

@wxn0brp/vql peers:

Package Required Purpose @wxn0brp/db-core yes Query types and the database interface @wxn0brp/falcon-frame no HTTP integration @wxn0brp/gate-warden no Permission backend

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import VQLProcessor, { VQLConfig, isVQLError } from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import { ValtheraCreate } from "@wxn0brp/db";

const main = ValtheraCreate("./data/main");
const processor = new VQLProcessor({ main });

// VQLS
const users = await processor.execute(
    `main users s.status="active" e.name=1 e.email=1`
);

// VQLR
const user = await processor.execute({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        findOne: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { _id: "u1" },
            select: ["name", "email"]
        }
    }
});

// Variables and user context
const mine = await processor.execute(
    {
        query: "main orders s.ownerId=$_me e._id=1 e.total=1",
        var: {}
    },
    { _id: "u1", role: "user" }
);

if (isVQLError(users)) {
    console.error(users.code, users.message);
}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
const processor = new VQLProcessor(
    { main },
    new VQLConfig({
        noCheckPermissions: true,       // default: permissions disabled
        strictSelect: false,            // must be true when permissions are enabled
        strictACL: false,               // allow parent-path fallback
        hidePath: false,                // hash paths passed to permValidFn
        permissionDeniedIfNoUser: true,
        allowEmptyAdd: true
    })
);

See Configuration for the full behavior of each option.

docs.title: Query lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Parse the query.
  2. Strings and { query: string } go through the VQLS parser.
  3. Objects are used as VQLR.
  4. Apply variables from the wrapper.
  5. Check the raw shape: r, or db + d.
  6. Expand predefined and custom variables.
  7. Validate the operation, collection, and relation structure.
  8. Check permissions when enabled.
  9. Execute:
  10. d runs a CRUD operation against one database.
  11. r loads records and relations across databases.
  12. Filter returned fields when permissions are enabled.
  13. Return the result or a VQLError.

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
VQL executes against ValtheraDB instances and adapter objects it recognizes. That opens four integration paths. LowAdapter is a special case: it is not a ValtheraCompatible implementation, and VQL detects it at runtime.

Approach Use when Native ValtheraDB instance The data lives in ValtheraDB LowAdapter You want full control over CRUD queries createValtheraAdapter Backing store is an API or a custom SDK AdapterBuilder You want per-operation, per-collection handlers

Databases are registered by name:

const processor = new VQLProcessor({
    main: valtheraDb,
    remote: apiAdapter,
    custom: lowAdapter
});

docs.title: LowAdapter
docs.text:
LowAdapter wraps a single resolver function and bypasses the CRUD executor:

import { LowAdapter } from "@wxn0brp/vql/helpers/lowAdapter";

const custom = new LowAdapter(async (query, user) => {
    const [operation] = Object.keys(query.d);
    return {
        operation,
        collection: query.d[operation].collection,
        user
    };
});

const processor = new VQLProcessor({ custom });

LowAdapter has only a resolver field. TypeScript expects ValtheraCompatible values in the constructor, so cast the entry when strict type checking is enabled: new VQLProcessor({ custom: custom as any }).

The resolver receives the validated CRUD query and the user context.

type LowResolver = (query: VQL_Query_CRUD, user: any) => Promise<any> | any;

Important properties:

  • Queries are still parsed, validated, and have variables expanded.
  • The permission layer is not applied. Authorize inside the resolver.
  • Relations are not routed through LowAdapter. Use a full ValtheraCompatible implementation for relation queries.
  • The resolver owns the result shape. VQL does not post-process it.

Use this for in-memory stores, proxies, or operations that do not map to a collection.

docs.title: createValtheraAdapter
docs.text:
createValtheraAdapter turns a set of resolver methods into a ValtheraCompatible object. The adapter covers the methods in the resolver interface below. Methods such as createIndex, removeIndex, and capabilities are not implemented and are missing at runtime.

import { createValtheraAdapter } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const apiAdapter = createValtheraAdapter({
    find: async query => {
        const res = await fetch(`/api/${query.collection}?q=` + encodeURIComponent(
            JSON.stringify(query.search)
        ));
        return await res.json();
    },
    findOne: async query => {
        const res = await fetch(`/api/${query.collection}/one?q=` + encodeURIComponent(
            JSON.stringify(query.search)
        ));
        const data = await res.json();
        return Array.isArray(data) ? (data[0] ?? null) : (data ?? null);
    },
    add: async query => {
        const res = await fetch(`/api/${query.collection}`, {
            method: "POST",
            headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
            body: JSON.stringify(query.data)
        });
        return await res.json();
    },
    count: async query => {
        const rows = await apiAdapter.find(query);
        return rows.length;
    }
});

docs.title: Resolver interface
docs.text:
interface ValtheraResolver {
    meta?: {
        type: "valthera" | "api" | "wrapper" | (string & {});
        version: string;
        description?: string;
        id?: string;
        displayName?: string;
        tags?: string[];
    };

    getCollections?: () => Promise<string[]>;
    issetCollection?: (collection: string) => Promise<boolean>;
    ensureCollection?: (collection: string) => Promise<boolean>;
    removeCollection?: (collection: string) => Promise<boolean>;

    add?: (query: VQueryT.Add) => Promise<Object>;
    find?: (query: VQueryT.Find) => Promise<Object[]>;
    findOne?: (query: VQueryT.FindOne) => Promise<Object | null>;

    update?: (query: VQueryT.Update) => Promise<Object[] | null>;
    updateOne?: (query: VQueryT.Update) => Promise<Object | null>;
    updateOneOrAdd?: (query: VQueryT.UpdateOneOrAdd) => Promise<UpdateOneOrAddResult>;
    toggleOne?: (query: VQueryT.ToggleOne) => Promise<ToggleOneResult>;

    count?: (query: VQueryT.Count) => Promise<number>;
    bulkAdd?: (query: VQueryT.BulkAdd) => Promise<Object[]>;

    remove?: (query: VQueryT.Remove) => Promise<Object | null>;
    removeOne?: (query: VQueryT.Remove) => Promise<Object | null>;
}

Missing methods are safe to omit. Calling one throws VQLOperationError with code VQL_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND and the message Unknown operation "Unimplemented method". The literal operation name is used because the adapter calls the shared missing-method guard.

The adapter exposes c(collection) through a Collection wrapper, so VQL can call collection methods without knowing which operations are implemented.

docs.title: extendedFind
docs.text:
createValtheraAdapter(resolver, extendedFind) accepts a second argument:

const adapter = createValtheraAdapter(resolver, true);

When extendedFind is true, the adapter handles a subset of find options on the client side:

  • dbFindOpts.reverse
  • dbFindOpts.limit (applied after reverse)
  • findOpts.select, findOpts.exclude, findOpts.transform

Other options such as offset, sortBy, aggregation, and grouping must be handled by the resolver itself.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
If resolver.meta is omitted, the adapter reports:

{ type: "api", version: "0.0.1" }

Use meta for tooling and debugging:

createValtheraAdapter({
    meta: {
        type: "api",
        version: "1.0.0",
        displayName: "Billing API",
        tags: ["billing"]
    },
    find: async query => { /* ... */ }
});

docs.title: AdapterBuilder
docs.text:
AdapterBuilder registers handlers per operation and collection:

import { AdapterBuilder } from "@wxn0brp/vql/helpers/apiAbstract";

const api = new AdapterBuilder((error, op, arg) => {
    console.error(`Adapter error in ${op}`, error);
});

api.find("users", async query => {
    return await dbUsers.find(query.search);
});

api.findOne("users", async query => {
    return await dbUsers.findOne(query.search);
});

api.add("users", async query => {
    return await dbUsers.add(query.data);
});

// Wildcard fallback for every collection
api.find("*", async query => {
    return await remoteSearch(query.collection, query.search);
});

const adapter = api.getAdapter();
const processor = new VQLProcessor({ main: adapter });

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Operation register(op, collection, fn) Generic registration add(collection, fn) add find(collection, fn) find findOne(collection, fn) findOne update(collection, fn) update updateOne(collection, fn) updateOne updateOneOrAdd(collection, fn) updateOneOrAdd toggleOne(collection, fn) toggleOne count(collection, fn) count bulkAdd(collection, fn) bulkAdd remove(collection, fn) remove removeOne(collection, fn) removeOne removeCollection(collection, fn) removeCollection

register takes any CRUD operation name from the Operation union.

docs.title: Resolution order
docs.text:
For a request, the builder looks up:

  1. ${operation}:${collection}
  2. ${operation}:*
  3. throws VQLHandlerMissingError if neither exists

If a handler throws, the builder calls the catchCb and resolves undefined. It does not rethrow. Make the callback log or rethrow deliberately if silent failures are not acceptable.

docs.title: Collection management
docs.text:
getAdapter() synthesizes:

  • getCollections() from the set of collections passed to register.
  • issetCollection() against that set.
  • ensureCollection() by adding to that set.

removeCollection is not wired by the builder in the current implementation. Assign a handler directly on the returned adapter if you need it:

const adapter = api.getAdapter();
adapter.removeCollection = async collection => {
    // remove the backing collection
    return true;
};

docs.title: extendedFind
docs.text:
getAdapter(extendedFind = true) passes the flag to createValtheraAdapter. Pass false if the backing API already applies reverse, limit, and selection:

const adapter = api.getAdapter(false);

docs.title: Choosing an approach
docs.text:
• Use ValtheraDB directly when possible. It gives you the full option set, transactions, and indexes without extra work.
  • Use createValtheraAdapter for a small, mostly read-only API.
  • Use AdapterBuilder when different collections have different backends.
  • Use LowAdapter only when you need to own the entire CRUD path and can handle permissions yourself.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
VQLConfig controls validation, visibility, and permission behavior. Every value has a default, so a processor can be created without a config object.

import VQLProcessor, { VQLConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const processor = new VQLProcessor(dbInstances, new VQLConfig({
    noCheckPermissions: false,
    strictSelect: true,
    strictACL: true
}));

The constructor also accepts a plain object:

const processor = new VQLProcessor(dbInstances, {
    noCheckPermissions: false,
    strictSelect: true
});

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Description noCheckPermissions true Disables the permission layer entirely strictSelect false Required to be true when permissions are enabled strictACL false Disables fallback from a missing entity to its parent path hidePath false Hashes permission paths before passing them to permValidFn permissionDeniedIfNoUser true Denies requests when the user context is falsy allowEmptyAdd true Allows add without a data payload

docs.title: noCheckPermissions
docs.text: The permission layer is off by default. When set to false, every operation is checked by permValidFn before execution, and returned records are filtered per field. LowAdapter databases are an exception: their resolver runs before the permission layer, so authorize inside the resolver. See Permissions.

docs.title: strictSelect
docs.text:
When permissions are enabled, strictSelect must be true. Constructing the config with noCheckPermissions: false and strictSelect: false throws VQLConfigError:

strictSelect must be true when permissions are enabled (noCheckPermissions: false).
Without strictSelect, nested fields without READ permission can be leaked.

The flag makes selection intent explicit. Field redaction itself is performed by the permission filter. For CRUD, an empty or omitted selection still returns full records. For relation queries, an empty selection becomes [] when strictSelect is true, which removes every field from the result.

docs.title: strictACL
docs.text:
Permission results can report reason: "entity-404", which means the path is not known to the permission backend.

  • strictACL: false (default): VQL retries the parent path, walking up from field to collection. The database-level retry applies to field paths only; collection operations such as add and remove have no parent fallback.
  • strictACL: true: the denial is final. No parent lookup is performed.

Use true when every path is registered explicitly and a missing entry should always mean "deny".

docs.title: hidePath
docs.text:
When true, the field passed to permValidFn is the SHA-256 hash of the JSON path instead of the JSON string itself:

// hidePath: false
field = '["main","users","email"]';

// hidePath: true
field = "a3f1...";  // sha256 of the JSON above

The original path is still available in args.path. Hashing keeps storage keys opaque but requires the permission backend to be populated with hashed keys.

Hashing works in Node.js and in browsers with WebCrypto.

docs.title: permissionDeniedIfNoUser
docs.text:
When true, a falsy user context causes an immediate denial. Only null triggers the denial in practice: execute() replaces undefined with the placeholder { _id: "null-null-null" }, so undefined continues with a fake identity. FF_VQL defaults the context to {} unless getUser is provided, and {} is truthy.

Pass an explicit user object in real applications. Return null from getUser to deny anonymous requests.

docs.title: allowEmptyAdd
docs.text:
When true (default), add may omit data or use {}. When false, the validator requires a non-empty object:

new VQLConfig({ allowEmptyAdd: false });

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Development

new VQLConfig({
    noCheckPermissions: true,
    strictSelect: false,
    strictACL: false,
    hidePath: false
});

Permission-aware

new VQLConfig({
    noCheckPermissions: false,
    strictSelect: true,
    strictACL: true,
    hidePath: false,
    permissionDeniedIfNoUser: true
});

Opaque paths

new VQLConfig({
    noCheckPermissions: false,
    strictSelect: true,
    strictACL: true,
    hidePath: true
});

docs.title: Per-query override
docs.text:
execute() accepts a third argument that overrides the processor config for a single query:

await processor.execute(query, user, new VQLConfig({
    noCheckPermissions: false,
    strictSelect: true
}));

The override is used as-is. Validation happens only in the VQLConfig constructor, so construct the config before passing it. A VQLConfig with permissions enabled and strictSelect: false throws before execute() is called. A plain object passed in this position is not validated.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: An invalid config produces a VQLConfigError with code VQL_CONFIG_INVALID and status code 500. See Errors.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
VQL never throws from VQLProcessor.execute() itself. It catches failures and returns a VQLError instance instead, so every call has a value-shaped result. Argument evaluation happens before the call: a new VQLConfig(...) with an invalid combination throws while the argument is built.

const result = await processor.execute(query, user);
if (result instanceof Error) {
    // VQLError
} else {
    // data
}

isVQLError narrows the type:

import { isVQLError } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

if (isVQLError(result)) {
    console.error(result.code, result.message);
}

Errors thrown by lower layers during execution are wrapped into VQLInternalError unless they are already a VQLError.

docs.title: Error shape
docs.text:
class VQLError extends ValtheraError {
    statusCode: number;
    code: string;
    suggestion?: string;
    context?: Record<string, unknown>;
    cause?: unknown;
}
Field Description name Class name, for example VQLParseError message Human-readable message code Stable code from VQLErrorCodes statusCode Suggested HTTP status suggestion Optional remediation hint context Optional structured details cause Original error, when wrapped

toJSON() returns name, code, message, optional suggestion, and optional context.

docs.title: Codes and classes
docs.text:
Code Class HTTP status Raised when VQL_QUERY_PARSE VQLParseError 400 String query cannot be parsed VQL_QUERY_VALIDATION VQLValidationError 400 Query structure fails validation VQL_DB_NOT_FOUND VQLDBNotFoundError 400 Database name is not registered VQL_PERMISSION_DENIED VQLPermissionDeniedError 403 Permission function denied the request VQL_RELATION_INVALID VQLRelationError 400 Reserved. Relation failures currently use validation, database, or permission errors VQL_CONFIG_INVALID VQLConfigError 500 Invalid config combination VQL_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND VQLOperationError 500 Unknown CRUD operation VQL_HANDLER_MISSING VQLHandlerMissingError 501 Adapter has no handler for operation and collection VQL_INTERNAL VQLInternalError 500 Unexpected failure during execution

All classes are exported from the package root:

import {
    VQLError,
    VQLParseError,
    VQLValidationError,
    VQLDBNotFoundError,
    VQLPermissionDeniedError,
    VQLRelationError,
    VQLConfigError,
    VQLOperationError,
    VQLHandlerMissingError,
    VQLInternalError,
    VQLErrorCodes,
    isVQLError
} from "@wxn0brp/vql";

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Database not registered

const result = await processor.execute({ db: "missing", d: { getCollections: {} } });
// VQLDBNotFoundError
// message: Database "missing" not found
// suggestion: Check that the database was registered with VQLProcessor
// context: { db: "missing" }

Invalid query shape

await processor.execute({ db: "main" } as any);
// VQLValidationError: Invalid VQL query structure. Must contain 'r' or 'db' and 'd'.

Missing collection

await processor.execute({ db: "main", d: { find: { collection: "" } } });
// VQLValidationError: CRUD operation 'find' must specify a non-empty 'collection' string.

Permission denied

// VQLPermissionDeniedError
// statusCode: 403
// message: Permission denied: operation not permitted

Missing adapter handler

// VQLHandlerMissingError
// statusCode: 501
// message: Unimplemented method: find:users
// suggestion: Register a handler for this operation+collection in AdapterBuilder

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text:
validateRaw runs before variable replacement and checks only the top-level shape:

Invalid VQL query structure. Must contain 'r' or 'db' and 'd'.

validateVql runs after variable replacement and performs the detailed checks:

  • The first key in d must be a known operation. Additional keys are ignored.
  • Collection names must be non-empty strings.
  • options, searchOpts, data, and add_arg must be objects when present.
  • search is required for findOne/f, update, updateOne, remove, removeOne, updateOneOrAdd, and toggleOne; it is optional for find and count.
  • updater is required for update, updateOne, and updateOneOrAdd.
  • limit must be a number when present.
  • select must be an object or an array.
  • datas must be an array.
  • Relation paths must be arrays of length two. Element types are not checked.
  • Nested relation select must be an array. Top-level r.select may be an object or an array.
  • Relation search and relations must be objects.

The full list of messages is in src/helpers/valid.ts.

docs.title: Error handling patterns
docs.text:
Fail the request

const result = await processor.execute(query, user);
if (isVQLError(result)) throw new Error(`${result.code}: ${result.message}`);

Map to an HTTP response

if (isVQLError(result)) {
    res.status(result.statusCode).json({
        err: true,
        msg: result.message,
        code: result.code,
        suggestion: result.suggestion,
        context: result.context
    });
}

FF_VQL does this automatically. See HTTP Integration.

Log and fall back

const result = await processor.execute(query, user);
if (isVQLError(result)) {
    logger.error(result.toJSON());
    return fallbackValue;
}
return result;

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
VQL includes an optional, path-based permission layer. It is disabled by default so that local scripts and trusted server code do not need any setup.

Permissions have two jobs:

  1. Check whether an operation may touch a database, collection, or field.
  2. Remove fields the user cannot read from returned records.

docs.title: Enabling permissions
docs.text:
import VQLProcessor, { VQLConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const processor = new VQLProcessor(
    dbInstances,
    new VQLConfig({
        noCheckPermissions: false,
        strictSelect: true,
        strictACL: true
    }),
    permValidFn
);

strictSelect must be true when permissions are enabled. Otherwise the config constructor throws VQLConfigError.

If no permValidFn is passed, the default function grants every request. That is useful while wiring the rest of the system, but it means noCheckPermissions: false alone does not secure anything.

docs.title: Permission function
docs.text:
type PermValidFn = (args: PermValidFnArgs) => Promise<ValidFnResult>;

interface PermValidFnArgs {
    field: string;    // JSON path, or sha256 hash when hidePath is true
    path: string[];   // original path segments
    p: number;        // CRUD bitmask
    user: any;        // user context passed to execute()
}

interface ValidFnResult {
    granted: boolean;
    via?: "resolver" | "gate-warden";
    reason?: string;
}

Minimal implementation:

import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

const permValidFn = async ({ path, p, user }) => {
    const [db, collection] = path;

    if (user?.role === "admin") {
        return { granted: true, via: "resolver", reason: "admin" };
    }

    if (db === "public" && collection === "posts" && p & PermCRUD.READ) {
        return { granted: true, via: "resolver", reason: "public-read" };
    }

    return { granted: false, via: "resolver", reason: "not-permitted" };
};

docs.title: CRUD flags
docs.text:
import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

enum PermCRUD {
    CREATE = 1,
    READ = 2,
    UPDATE = 4,
    DELETE = 8,
    COLLECTION = 16
}

Flags are bit values. Combine them with | and test them with &.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
Collection-level checks use:

[database, collection]

Field-level checks use:

[database, collection, ...fieldPath]

For example, selecting users.email from main produces:

["main", "users", "email"]

When hidePath is true, the field argument is the SHA-256 hash of the JSON encoded path. The path argument always contains the original segments.

docs.title: Operation mapping
docs.text:
Operation Collection check Field checks find, findOne, f READ search paths: READ add CREATE none update, updateOne none search paths: READ, updater paths: UPDATE remove, removeOne DELETE none updateOneOrAdd CREATE search paths: READ, updater paths: UPDATE toggleOne CREATE and DELETE none count READ search paths: READ bulkAdd CREATE none ensureCollection, issetCollection, removeCollection, getCollections COLLECTION none

Notes:

  • add and bulkAdd do not validate the payload fields. Validate user input separately if field-level write limits matter.
  • remove does not check search fields, only the collection DELETE flag.
  • Every required check must pass.
  • Collection operations use the collection name as part of the path. For getCollections the collection segment is an empty string.

docs.title: Operator paths
docs.text:
Search and updater objects are flattened to field paths. Operator keys such as $gt, $in, and $or are skipped, so a condition on age is checked as age, not $gt.age.

$subset is an exception: it means "the following path is literal data", so the segments after $subset are kept.

{ $gt: { age: 18 } }              // path: ["main","users","age"]
{ $subset: { $ref: "abc" } }      // path: ["main","users","$ref"]

docs.title: Field filtering
docs.text:
After an operation returns records, VQL walks every path in each object and asks for READ permission. Denied paths are removed from the result.

// Stored record
{ _id: "1", name: "Alice", email: "a@x.com", salary: 9000 }

// User can read _id, name, email but not salary
{ _id: "1", name: "Alice", email: "a@x.com" }

Filtering applies to:

  • find, findOne
  • add, bulkAdd (the returned records)
  • update, updateOne, remove, removeOne
  • updateOneOrAdd, toggleOne (the data field)

Relation results are not field-filtered after loading. The permission layer checks the relation path, search fields, and selected fields before execution, so omit the relation key or select only permitted fields. count returns a number and is not filtered.

docs.title: Fallback and strictACL
docs.text:
A permission function can report reason: "entity-404" when the requested path is not registered.

  • strictACL: false (default): a denied field path is retried with parent paths, walking up from field to collection to database. Collection-level checks do not fall back to the database.
  • strictACL: true: the denial is final.

This allows a field-level grant to live on a parent path:

// Grant all fields under main/users, strictACL: false
permValidFn = async ({ path }) => {
    if (path[0] === "main" && path[1] === "users") {
        return { granted: true };
    }
    return { granted: false, reason: "entity-404" };
};

With strictACL: true, the same function still grants main/users and its fields because the prefix matches. A function that only returns entity-404 for unknown paths would deny them instead.

docs.title: Missing user
docs.text: If permissionDeniedIfNoUser is true (default) and the user context is falsy, the request is denied before any check. In practice only null triggers the denial: execute() replaces undefined with the placeholder { _id: "null-null-null" }, and the HTTP helper defaults to {} when no getUser function is provided. Both values are truthy but usually not what you want. Always pass a real context in production and return null from getUser for anonymous requests.

docs.title: PermissionResolverEngine
docs.text:
PermissionResolverEngine builds a PermValidFn from path matchers. The first matching resolver wins. If nothing matches, the request is denied.

import { PermissionResolverEngine } from "@wxn0brp/vql/permissions/resolver";
import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

const engine = new PermissionResolverEngine();

// Exact path
engine.addResolver("main/users/email", async ({ user }) => {
    return user?.role === "admin";
});

// Any password field
engine.addResolver("password", async () => false, "endsWith");

// Admin access to a collection
engine.addResolver("main/users", async ({ user, p }) => {
    return user?.role === "admin" || (p & PermCRUD.READ) !== 0;
});

// Regular expression
engine.addResolver(/^main\/public\//, async () => true);

// Custom function
engine.addResolver(
    (path, segments) => segments[1] === "posts",
    async ({ user }) => !!user
);

const permValidFn = engine.create();

docs.title: Matchers
docs.text:
Matcher Example Description string "main/users/email" String mode, exact by default RegExp /password$/ test() against the joined path function (path, segments) => boolean Custom predicate, may be async

String modes:

engine.addResolver("password", resolver, "endsWith");     // main/users/password
engine.addResolver("main/", resolver, "startsWith");      // main/users
engine.addResolver("secret", resolver, "includes");       // config/secret_key
engine.addResolver("main/users/email", resolver);         // exact

The joined path uses / between segments.

docs.title: Resolver errors
docs.text: If a resolver throws, the engine logs the error with console.error and denies the request with reason: "resolver-error". Denials from other resolvers stop the search; only a missing match (no-resolver-match) continues.

docs.title: Gate Warden fallback
docs.text:
createWithGw falls back to Gate Warden only when no custom resolver matched:

import { GateWarden } from "@wxn0brp/gate-warden";

const gw = new GateWarden(gwDb);
const engine = new PermissionResolverEngine();
engine.addResolver("password", async () => false, "endsWith");
const permValidFn = engine.createWithGw(gw);

docs.title: createGwValidFn
docs.text:
If you do not need custom resolvers, use Gate Warden directly:

import { createGwValidFn } from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import { GateWarden } from "@wxn0brp/gate-warden";

const gw = new GateWarden(gwDb);
const permValidFn = createGwValidFn(gw);

createGwValidFn calls:

gw.hasAccess(user._id ?? user.id, args.field, args.p);

Gate Warden loads the user from its own database. A user that does not exist there is reported as user-404 and access is denied, even if the VQL context contains a valid user object. Register users and rules in the Gate Warden database, and hash paths with the same hidePath setting used by VQL.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
import VQLProcessor, { VQLConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import { PermissionResolverEngine } from "@wxn0brp/vql/permissions/resolver";
import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

const engine = new PermissionResolverEngine();

// Never expose password hashes.
engine.addResolver("password", async () => false, "endsWith");

// Users can read all user fields except passwords.
// Only admins can update or delete.
engine.addResolver("main/users", async ({ p, user }) => {
    if (user?.role === "admin") return true;
    return (p & PermCRUD.READ) !== 0;
}, "startsWith");

const processor = new VQLProcessor(
    dbInstances,
    new VQLConfig({
        noCheckPermissions: false,
        strictSelect: true,
        strictACL: true
    }),
    engine.create()
);

const user = { _id: "user123", role: "user" };
const result = await processor.execute(
    `main users s._id=$_me e.name=1 e.email=1`,
    user
);

docs.title: LowAdapter bypass
docs.text: LowAdapter resolvers run before the permission check. If you mount a LowAdapter, the permission layer is not applied. Do the authorization inside the resolver. See Adapters.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text: Relations let one query join records across collections and databases. VQL passes the relation description to ValtheraDB, which loads the related records and attaches them to each parent record under the relation key.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
A relation query has no db + d pair. It uses the r key directly:

{
    r: {
        path: ["orders_db", "orders"],
        search: { status: "pending" },
        relations: {
            customer: {
                path: ["users_db", "users"],
                pk: "customerId",
                fk: "_id",
                select: ["name", "email"]
            }
        },
        many: true,
        select: [["_id"], ["customer", "name"]]
    }
}

path is [database, collection] and must reference a database registered with the processor. search and relations are required objects. They may be empty, but they must be present.

docs.title: Relation options
docs.text:
Each entry in relations is keyed by the output field name and accepts:

Option Default Description path required [database, collection] of the related records pk _id Field on the parent record used for the join fk _id Field on the related record used for the join type "1" Relation type: 1, 11, 1n, nm, n1 as relation key Field name used for the joined output select all fields Fields to keep on the related record dbFindOpts {} Database find options for the related query relations none Nested relations on the related record through none Pivot table description for nm

docs.title: Select
docs.text:
select is an array of field names on the related record. The join field is added automatically and removed from the result unless it was selected explicitly.

customer: {
    path: ["users_db", "users"],
    pk: "customerId",
    fk: "_id",
    select: ["name", "email"]
}

docs.title: Types
Many-to-many
docs.text:
type: "nm" requires through:

{
    path: ["main", "tags"],
    type: "nm",
    pk: "_id",
    fk: "_id",
    through: {
        table: "post_tags",
        db: "main",       // optional, defaults to the related collection's database
        pk: "postId",     // parent id stored in the pivot
        fk: "tagId"       // related id stored in the pivot
    }
}

The pivot collection is queried for rows whose through.pk matches the parent pk. The through.fk values are then resolved against the related collection using fk.

docs.title: Nested relations
docs.text:
{
    r: {
        path: ["main", "orders"],
        search: {},
        relations: {
            customer: {
                path: ["main", "users"],
                pk: "customerId",
                relations: {
                    company: {
                        path: ["main", "companies"],
                        pk: "companyId",
                        fk: "_id"
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Nested relation output is attached to the related record. Top-level select paths address it through the relation key: ["customer", "company", "name"].

docs.title: Multi-database
docs.text: Every path selects its own database. through.db selects the database for a pivot collection and defaults to the database in the relation path. Only the databases in path are checked before execution. An unregistered through.db fails later during the pivot lookup instead of raising VQLDBNotFoundError.

docs.title: Top-level query options
docs.text:
Option Description many true runs find, false (default) runs findOne options DbFindOpts for the parent query select Field paths to keep, as an array of segment arrays (string[][])

select accepts nested paths for joined objects:

select: [["_id"], ["customer", "name"], ["items"]]

For array relations such as 1n and nm, select the relation key as a whole. Field picking does not traverse arrays, so ["items", "price"] would produce undefined fields instead of filtering each item.

Top-level relation select must use segment arrays, as shown above. The validator also accepts an object, but the relation engine does not convert it in VQLR: the object is flattened to top-level keys and the lookup throws VQLInternalError. Build the query in VQLS, where e. is converted before execution.

docs.title: VQLS syntax
docs.text:
In VQLS, a relation query starts when the body contains an r. key. The relation path defaults to [current database, relation name]:

db orders s.status="pending"
r.customer.path=["users_db","users"]
r.customer.pk="customerId"
r.customer.fk="_id"
r.customer.select=["name","email"]
r.items.path=["orders_db","items"]
r.items.type="1n"
r.items.pk="_id"
r.items.fk="orderId"
many=true
e._id=1 e.customer.name=1 e.items=1

The db and c keys are shorthand for the two path segments:

r.customer.db="users_db" r.customer.c="users"

r.x.select must be a JSON array. A dotted object such as r.customer.select.name=1 fails validation because relation selects are arrays.

Root relation options use their plain names:

many=true
options.limit=10

Do not write r.many=true or r.options.limit=10. The r. prefix always creates a relation entry, so those keys would be interpreted as relations named many and options.

Top-level relation select keeps nested paths:

e._id=1 e.customer.name=1 e.items=1

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
When permissions are enabled, relation queries are checked before execution:

  • The relation path requires READ.
  • Every search field requires READ.
  • Every selected field requires READ.
  • Nested relations are checked recursively with the same rules, except that their own search is replaced with {} during the recursive check, so nested search fields are not checked.

The permission path is built as [database, collection, ...fieldPath] for flat string paths. Segment-array selects such as [["customer", "name"]] are passed as a single array element instead of being flattened, so prefer flat field paths when permissions are enabled. See Permissions.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Typical validation errors:

Message Cause Relation query 'r' must have a 'path' property with an array of two strings. Missing or malformed path Relation query 'r.search' must be an object. Missing search Relation query 'r' must have a 'relations' object. Missing relations Relation 'x' must have a 'path' property with an array of two strings. Bad nested path Relation 'x' has an invalid 'select' property; it must be an array. Object select on a relation Database "x" not found Unregistered database in a path

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Runnable patterns for common tasks. All examples assume a processor created as described in Getting Started.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
import VQLProcessor, { VQLConfig, isVQLError } from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import type { VQLUQ } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/vql";
import { ValtheraCreate } from "@wxn0brp/db";

const main = ValtheraCreate("./data/main");
const analytics = ValtheraCreate("./data/analytics");

const processor = new VQLProcessor(
    { main, analytics },
    new VQLConfig({ noCheckPermissions: true })
);

const run = async <T = any>(query: VQLUQ<T>): Promise<T> => {
    const result = await processor.execute<T>(query);
    if (isVQLError(result)) throw result;
    return result as T;
};

docs.title: Create and read
docs.text:
await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        add: {
            collection: "users",
            data: { _id: "u1", name: "Alice", email: "alice@example.com", age: 30 }
        }
    }
});

const user = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        findOne: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { _id: "u1" },
            select: ["name", "email"]
        }
    }
});

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
const page = 2;
const pageSize = 20;

const rows = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        find: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { status: "active" },
            options: {
                limit: pageSize,
                offset: (page - 1) * pageSize,
                sortBy: [{ field: "name", asc: true }]
            },
            select: ["_id", "name", "email"]
        }
    }
});

const total = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: { count: { collection: "users", search: { status: "active" } } }
});

Use options.limit, not the top-level limit field.

docs.title: Partial update
docs.text:
await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        updateOne: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { _id: "u1" },
            updater: {
                name: "Alice Smith",
                $set: { profile: { lastLogin: { __: "_now" } } }
            },
            select: ["name", "profile.lastLogin"]
        }
    }
});

docs.title: Soft delete
docs.text:
await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        updateOne: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { _id: "u1" },
            updater: { deleted: true, deletedAt: { __: "_now" } }
        }
    }
});

const activeUsers = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        find: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { deleted: false }
        }
    }
});

Records created before the flag existed do not have deleted. Backfill them, or search with { $not: { deleted: true } } to include missing fields.

docs.title: Atomic counter
docs.text:
await run({
    db: "analytics",
    d: {
        updateOne: {
            collection: "counters",
            search: { _id: "page-views" },
            updater: { $inc: { value: 1 } }
        }
    }
});

For an upsert:

await run({
    db: "analytics",
    d: {
        updateOneOrAdd: {
            collection: "counters",
            search: { _id: "page-views" },
            updater: { $inc: { value: 1 } },
            add_arg: { _id: "page-views" }
        }
    }
});

docs.title: Upsert a profile
docs.text:
const { data, type } = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        updateOneOrAdd: {
            collection: "profiles",
            search: { userId: "u1" },
            updater: { lastSeen: { __: "_now" } },
            add_arg: { userId: "u1", displayName: "Alice" },
            select: ["userId", "displayName", "lastSeen"]
        }
    }
});

console.log(type); // "added" or "updated"

docs.title: Toggle a favorite
docs.text:
const result = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        toggleOne: {
            collection: "favorites",
            search: { userId: "u1", itemId: "p42" }
        }
    }
});

console.log(result.type); // "added" or "removed"
console.log(result.data);

docs.title: Bulk import
docs.text:
const inserted = await run({
    db: "main",
    d: {
        bulkAdd: {
            collection: "products",
            datas: [
                { _id: "p1", name: "Laptop", price: 1200 },
                { _id: "p2", name: "Mouse", price: 25 }
            ]
        }
    }
});

docs.title: Join orders with customers and items
docs.text:
const orders = await run({
    r: {
        path: ["main", "orders"],
        search: { status: "pending" },
        many: true,
        relations: {
            customer: {
                path: ["main", "users"],
                type: "1",
                pk: "customerId",
                fk: "_id",
                select: ["name", "email"]
            },
            items: {
                path: ["main", "items"],
                type: "1n",
                pk: "_id",
                fk: "orderId",
                select: ["name", "price", "quantity"]
            }
        },
        options: { limit: 50 },
        select: [["_id"], ["customer", "name"], ["items"]]
    }
});

docs.title: Multi-database lookup
docs.text:
const enriched = await run({
    r: {
        path: ["main", "orders"],
        search: { _id: "o1" },
        relations: {
            customer: {
                path: ["users", "users"],
                pk: "customerId",
                fk: "_id",
                select: ["name"]
            },
            shipment: {
                path: ["logistics", "shipments"],
                pk: "_id",
                fk: "orderId",
                select: ["status", "trackingNumber"]
            }
        }
    }
});

Register every referenced database:

new VQLProcessor({ main, users, logistics });

docs.title: Authenticated query with permissions
docs.text:
import { PermissionResolverEngine } from "@wxn0brp/vql/permissions/resolver";
import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

const engine = new PermissionResolverEngine();

engine.addResolver("password", async () => false, "endsWith");

engine.addResolver("main/orders", async ({ p, user }) => {
    if (user?.role === "admin") return true;
    return (p & PermCRUD.READ) !== 0;
}, "startsWith");

const secure = new VQLProcessor(
    { main },
    new VQLConfig({
        noCheckPermissions: false,
        strictSelect: true,
        strictACL: true
    }),
    engine.create()
);

const orders = await secure.execute(
    "main orders s.ownerId=$_me e._id=1 e.total=1",
    { _id: "u1", role: "user" }
);

docs.title: HTTP endpoint
docs.text:
import { FalconFrame } from "@wxn0brp/falcon-frame";
import { FF_VQL } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const app = new FalconFrame();

FF_VQL(app, secure, {
    path: "/vql",
    getUser: async req => {
        const token = req.header("Authorization")?.replace("Bearer ", "");
        if (!token) return null;
        return verifyToken(token); // your implementation
    },
    getQuery: async req => ({
        query: req.body.query,
        var: req.body.var
    })
});

app.l(3000);

Request:

{
    "query": "main orders s.ownerId=$_me e._id=1 e.total=1",
    "var": {}
}

docs.title: Step 1: Create databases
docs.text:
import VQLProcessor from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import { ValtheraCreate } from "@wxn0brp/db";

const usersDb = ValtheraCreate("./data/users");
const productsDb = ValtheraCreate("./data/products");

await usersDb.add({
    collection: "users",
    data: { _id: "user1", name: "Alice", age: 30, role: "admin" }
});

await usersDb.add({
    collection: "users",
    data: { _id: "user2", name: "Bob", age: 25, role: "user" }
});

await productsDb.add({
    collection: "items",
    data: { _id: "item1", name: "Laptop", price: 1200 }
});

const processor = new VQLProcessor({
    users: usersDb,
    products: productsDb
});

The keys in the object are the database names used by queries.

docs.title: Step 2: Query with VQLR
docs.text:
VQLR is the object form. It is explicit and works well with TypeScript.

import type { VQLUQ } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/vql";

const query: VQLUQ = {
    db: "users",
    d: {
        find: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { $gt: { age: 20 } },
            select: { name: 1, age: 1 },
            options: { sortBy: [{ field: "age", asc: true }] }
        }
    }
};

const result = await processor.execute(query);
// [{ name: "Bob", age: 25 }, { name: "Alice", age: 30 }]

docs.title: Step 3: Query with VQLS
docs.text:
VQLS is the string form. It is shorter and works well in scripts, logs, and CLI tools.

const result = await processor.execute(
    `products items s.$gt.price=100 e.name=1 e.price=1`
);
// [{ name: "Laptop", price: 1200 }]

Comparison operators have shorthand:

await processor.execute(`users users s.age>20 e.name=1`);
await processor.execute(`users users s.age>=20 e.name=1`);

docs.title: Step 4: Write data
docs.text:
// Insert
await processor.execute(`users +users d.name="Charlie" d.age=22 d.role="user"`);

// Update one record
await processor.execute(
    `users ~users! s._id="user2" u.age=26 u.updatedAt=$_now`
);

// Upsert
await processor.execute(
    `users ?users s._id="user3" u.name="Dana" u.age=28`
);

// Delete one record
await processor.execute(`users -users! s._id="user3"`);

// Count
const active = await processor.execute(`users #users s.role="admin"`);

docs.title: Step 5: Variables
docs.text:
Predefined variables are available in both syntaxes:

Variable Value _me User id _user Full user object _now Milliseconds timestamp _nowShort Seconds timestamp __now Milliseconds as a string __nowShort Seconds as a string 
const result = await processor.execute(
    {
        query: `users users s.age>$minAge e.name=1`,
        var: { minAge: 24 }
    },
    { _id: "viewer1", role: "user" }
);

In VQLR, use reference objects:

await processor.execute({
    db: "users",
    d: {
        add: {
            collection: "audit",
            data: { action: "login", userId: { __: "_me" }, at: { __: "_now" } }
        }
    }
});

docs.title: Step 6: Relations
docs.text:
Relation queries join data across collections and databases.

await productsDb.add({
    collection: "orders",
    data: { _id: "order1", userId: "user1", itemId: "item1", quantity: 1 }
});

const orders = await processor.execute({
    r: {
        path: ["products", "orders"],
        search: {},
        many: true,
        relations: {
            user: {
                path: ["users", "users"],
                pk: "userId",
                fk: "_id",
                select: ["name", "role"]
            },
            item: {
                path: ["products", "items"],
                pk: "itemId",
                fk: "_id",
                select: ["name", "price"]
            }
        },
        select: [["_id"], ["user", "name"], ["item", "name"]]
    }
});

The same query in VQLS:

products orders
r.user.path=["users","users"]
r.user.pk="userId"
r.user.fk="_id"
r.user.select=["name","role"]
r.item.path=["products","items"]
r.item.pk="itemId"
r.item.fk="_id"
r.item.select=["name","price"]
many=true
e._id=1 e.user.name=1 e.item.name=1

See Relations for relation types and many-to-many joins.

docs.title: Step 7: Collection management
docs.text:
await processor.execute(`users ensureCollection logs`);
const collections = await processor.execute(`users getCollections`);
await processor.execute(`users removeCollection logs`);

docs.title: Step 8: Enable permissions
docs.text:
Permissions are off by default. To enable them, pass a config and a permission function:

import { VQLConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import { PermissionResolverEngine } from "@wxn0brp/vql/permissions/resolver";
import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

const engine = new PermissionResolverEngine();
engine.addResolver("password", async () => false, "endsWith");
engine.addResolver("users/users", async ({ p, user }) => {
    if (user?.role === "admin") return true;
    return (p & PermCRUD.READ) !== 0;
}, "startsWith");

const secureProcessor = new VQLProcessor(
    { users: usersDb, products: productsDb },
    new VQLConfig({
        noCheckPermissions: false,
        strictSelect: true,
        strictACL: true
    }),
    engine.create()
);

const user = { _id: "user1", role: "admin" };
const result = await secureProcessor.execute(
    `users users s.role="admin" e.name=1 e.role=1`,
    user
);

See Permissions for path rules, hashing, and Gate Warden.

docs.title: Step 9: Handle errors
docs.text:
execute() returns a VQLError instead of throwing:

import { isVQLError } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const result = await processor.execute(`missing users`);
if (isVQLError(result)) {
    console.error(result.code);       // VQL_DB_NOT_FOUND
    console.error(result.message);
    console.error(result.suggestion);
}

See Errors.

docs.title: Step 10: Expose over HTTP
docs.text:
import { FalconFrame } from "@wxn0brp/falcon-frame";
import { FF_VQL } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const app = new FalconFrame();
FF_VQL(app, processor);
app.l(3000);

The endpoint accepts:

{ "query": "users users s.role=\"admin\"" }

and returns:

{ "err": false, "result": [] }

docs.title: The query returns an error object instead of throwing
docs.text:
VQLProcessor.execute() never throws for query failures. It returns a VQLError. Check the result:

import { isVQLError } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

const result = await processor.execute(query, user);
if (isVQLError(result)) {
    console.error(result.code, result.message, result.suggestion);
}

See Errors.

docs.title: Database "x" not found
docs.text:
The first argument to VQLProcessor is a name map:

new VQLProcessor({
    main: dbMain,
    analytics: dbAnalytics
});

Queries use those names exactly:

main users

Relation paths also use registered names: path: ["analytics", "events"].

docs.title: "Invalid VQL query structure. Must contain 'r' or 'db' and 'd'."
docs.text:
The object has neither r nor a db + d pair.

// Invalid
{ db: "main" }

// Valid
{ db: "main", d: { find: { collection: "users" } } }
{ r: { path: ["main", "users"], search: {}, relations: {} } }

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text: Message Fix CRUD operation 'x' must specify a non-empty 'collection' string. Add a collection name 'findOne' operation requires a 'search' object. Add search: {} even for a match-all 'update' operation requires an 'updater' object. Add updater 'bulkAdd' operation requires a 'datas' array. Use an array 'find' operation 'select' property must be an object or an array. Use ["name"] or { name: 1 }. The operation name is part of the message Relation query 'r.search' must be an object. Add search: {} Relation query 'r' must have a 'relations' object. Add relations: {} Relation 'x' has an invalid 'select' property; it must be an array. Use select: ["name"] Database "x" not found Register the name in the processor

docs.title: Query returns an empty array
docs.text:
Check the search shape. Some operators expect nested field objects:

// Wrong: this asks for a field called "$gt"
{ "$gt": 18 }

// Right
{ $gt: { age: 18 } }

Other causes:

  • s.age>18 in VQLS becomes { $gt: { age: 18 } }, not a plain equality.
  • Numeric strings must be quoted: s.externalId="123".
  • select does not filter records, it only projects fields.
  • options.limit limits results. A top-level limit is ignored.
  • If you sort with sortBy and also use select, include the sort field in the selection. Removing it can make the sort ineffective.
  • A relation query with many: false returns one record or null.

docs.title: Fields are missing from the result
docs.text:
• select keeps only the listed fields.
  • searchOpts.exclude removes fields.
  • With permissions enabled, fields without READ are removed.
  • VQLS e.profile.city=1 selects the whole profile for CRUD operations. Use VQLR for a nested CRUD selection.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text:
Common causes:

  1. No user context. permissionDeniedIfNoUser defaults to true. Only null is denied; undefined is replaced by the placeholder { _id: "null-null-null" } and continues with a fake identity. Always pass a real user object.
  2. strictSelect missing. Enabling permissions without strictSelect: true throws VQLConfigError at construction.
  3. Path mismatch. Permission paths are [database, collection, ...field]. Check the exact spelling and casing.
  4. hidePath mismatch. With hidePath: true, args.field is a SHA-256 hash. Rules registered with plain paths will not match.
  5. No resolver match. PermissionResolverEngine denies when nothing matches. Add a startsWith or regex matcher, or use createWithGw.
  6. Gate Warden user missing. createGwValidFn loads the user from the Gate Warden database. A missing user is reported as user-404.
  7. entity-404 with strictACL: true. Register the exact path or disable strict ACL to allow parent fallback.

Inspect the permission arguments:

const permValidFn = async args => {
    console.dir(args);
    return { granted: false };
};

docs.title: Permission checks do not run
docs.text:
• noCheckPermissions defaults to true. Set it to false.
  • LowAdapter resolvers bypass the permission layer. Authorize inside the resolver.
  • If you pass a custom permValidFn that always returns { granted: true }, every request is allowed.

docs.title: Relation errors
docs.text:
• path must be exactly two strings: ["db", "collection"].
  • search and relations must exist, even when empty.
  • Relation select is an array. In VQLS use JSON: r.items.select=["name"].
  • A missing database in any relation path throws VQLDBNotFoundError. A bad through.db is not pre-checked and fails later with VQLInternalError.
  • type: "nm" requires through.table, through.pk, and through.fk.

See Relations.

docs.title: VQLS parsing surprises
docs.text:
Input Result Reason db removeOne users! s._id="1" Collection users! Explicit operations do not strip ! s.active= followed by another key Wrong pair Empty value consumes the next token s.name=Alice String "Alice" Unquoted values stay strings s.id=123 Number 123 Quote to keep as string s.date=null String "null" Use JSON: s={"date":null} s.a.b>1 { $gt: { a: { b: 1 } } } Operators are applied operator-first s={"a": 1} Parsed incorrectly JSON values must be compact r.orders.search.status="pending" Accepted but not applied The relation loader ignores per-relation search e.profile.city=1 Selects profile CRUD selects collapse to top level

Quoted values are needed for spaces, =, <, and >.

docs.title: HTTP endpoint returns 500
docs.text:
• The processor is returning a VQLInternalError from an unexpected exception. Enable logging at DEBUG and inspect the error.
  • A custom adapter threw. AdapterBuilder swallows handler errors into undefined; pass a catchCb that logs.
  • Falcon Frame did not parse the body. Make sure the request is JSON and the body uses the query key, or provide getQuery.

A 501 means no adapter handler exists for that operation and collection. Register one or add a "*" handler.

docs.title: TypeScript cannot find VQLUQ or VQL_Query
docs.text:
Types are published under subpaths, not the package root:

import type { VQLUQ, VQL_Query } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/vql";

Permission types:

import { PermCRUD } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/perm";

docs.title: Debug logging
docs.text:
import { VQLLogger, VQLLogLevel } from "@wxn0brp/vql";

VQLLogger.logLevel = VQLLogLevel.DEBUG;

The logger prints incoming queries, expanded queries, validation failures, and internal errors. It may include user data, so disable it in production.

docs.title: Still stuck
docs.text:
Capture the failing query, the config, and the user context. Run the query through processor._preProcessQuery(query, user) to see whether it fails before execution:

const prepared = processor._preProcessQuery(query, user);
console.dir(prepared, { depth: null });

docs.title: Browser Usage
docs.text:
A browser cannot open a filesystem-backed ValtheraDB. Run the VQLProcessor on a server and use @wxn0brp/vql-client, or embed the processor in the same origin and communicate over BroadcastChannel.

import { fetchVQL, VConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql-client";

VConfig.url = "http://localhost:48652/VQL";
VConfig.headers = { Authorization: "Bearer TOKEN" };

const users = await fetchVQL("main users s.status=$status", { status: "active" });

For the embedded setup, open a channel named VQL: send { type: "vql", data: { id, query } } and receive { type: "vql-" + id, data: result }. Adapters are listed with { type: "getAdapters" }. This only works between same-origin pages.

The VQL-dev panel uses both modes: HTTP by default, or ?p=web for the channel. See VQL-dev/front for a reference implementation.

For permission path hashing, the browser uses WebCrypto and produces the same SHA-256 hex digest as Node.js. Never ship database credentials or a permissive permValidFn in a browser bundle.

docs.title: HTTP API Integration
docs.text: Expose a VQLProcessor as an HTTP endpoint with Falcon Frame.

docs.title: Server setup
docs.text:
import { FalconFrame } from "@wxn0brp/falcon-frame";
import { VQLProcessor, VQLConfig, FF_VQL } from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import { ValtheraCreate } from "@wxn0brp/db";

const db = ValtheraCreate("./data/my-db");
const processor = new VQLProcessor(
    { main: db },
    new VQLConfig({ noCheckPermissions: false, strictSelect: true }),
    permValidFn
);

const app = new FalconFrame();

FF_VQL(app, processor);

app.l(3000);

FF_VQL registers a POST route. The default path is /VQL.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
FF_VQL(router, processor, {
    path: "/VQL",
    getUser: async (req, res) => user,
    getQuery: async (req, res) => query
});
Option Default Description path "/VQL" Route path getUser () => ({}) Build the user context from the request getQuery req.body?.query Extract the query from the request dev ignored Deprecated, has no effect

The default context is {}. That is truthy, so permissionDeniedIfNoUser does not trigger, but no roles or ids are available. Always provide a real getUser for protected endpoints.

docs.title: Request format
docs.text:
By default the handler reads req.body.query:

{
    "query": "main users s.status=\"active\" e.name=1"
}

The endpoint accepts VQLS strings only. A VQLR object passed as query is sent to the string parser and fails with VQL_QUERY_PARSE. Handle VQLR on the server, or add a custom route that calls processor.execute directly.

To send variables with a string query, return the wrapper from getQuery:

FF_VQL(app, processor, {
    getQuery: async req => ({
        query: req.body.query,
        var: req.body.var
    })
});

Client request:

{
    "query": "main users s.role=$role",
    "var": { "role": "admin" }
}

docs.title: User context
docs.text:
FF_VQL(app, processor, {
    getUser: async (req, res) => {
        const token = req.header("Authorization")?.replace("Bearer ", "");
        if (!token) return null;

        const payload = verifyToken(token);  // your auth implementation
        const user = await db.findOne({ collection: "users", search: { _id: payload.sub } });
        return user;
    }
});

The returned object is passed to processor.execute() and is available in permission resolvers and in predefined variables ($_me, $_user).

Returning null triggers permissionDeniedIfNoUser when permissions are enabled. undefined is replaced by execute() with the placeholder { _id: "null-null-null" } and continues with a fake identity, so return null for anonymous requests.

docs.title: Custom query extraction
docs.text:
FF_VQL(app, processor, {
    getQuery: async req => {
        const query = req.query.q;
        return query ? JSON.parse(query) : req.body.query;
    }
});

docs.title: Custom routing
docs.text:
For more control, use the handler directly:

import { createVqlRouteHandler } from "@wxn0brp/vql/helpers/falconFrame";

const handler = createVqlRouteHandler(processor, {
    getUser: async req => ({ _id: "user123" })
});

app.post("/custom-vql", handler);

docs.title: Response format
docs.text:
Success

{
    "err": false,
    "result": { }
}

Error

{
    "err": true,
    "msg": "Permission denied: operation not permitted",
    "c": 403,
    "code": "VQL_PERMISSION_DENIED",
    "suggestion": "Check permissions for the user and collection",
    "context": { "reason": "operation not permitted" }
}

suggestion and context appear only when the error provides them.

The HTTP status is set from VQLError.statusCode. Unexpected errors are wrapped by wrapAdapterError and returned with status 500.

Status Typical cause 400 Parse or validation error, unknown database, invalid relation 403 Permission denied 500 Invalid config, unknown operation, unexpected failure 501 Missing adapter handler

docs.title: Authentication notes
docs.text:
• The integration does not implement authentication. getUser is the hook.
  • The route does not add CORS headers. Configure them in Falcon Frame if the client runs on a different origin.
  • Do not expose noCheckPermissions: true publicly. It grants full database access to anyone who can reach the endpoint.
  • Return a stable user shape with _id (or id) so Gate Warden and built-in variables work.

docs.title: Frontend client
docs.text:
The companion client is @wxn0brp/vql-client.

npm install @wxn0brp/vql-client

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
import { VConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql-client";

VConfig.url = "http://localhost:3000/VQL";
VConfig.headers = { Authorization: "Bearer TOKEN" };
VConfig.body = {};
VConfig.hookContext = {};

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import { fetchVQL, V } from "@wxn0brp/vql-client";

// VQLS with variables
const users = await fetchVQL(
    "main users s.status=$status",
    { status: "active" }
);

// Tagged template
const item = await V`main items! s._id="item-001"`;

// VQLR object, only with a server that accepts objects
// (FF_VQL expects a VQLS string)
const result = await fetchVQL({
    db: "main",
    d: { find: { collection: "users", search: { role: "admin" } } }
});

// Hook context and fetch options
const data = await fetchVQL(
    "main users s.role=$role",
    { role: "admin" },
    { requestId: "123" },
    { signal: abortController.signal }
);

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
VConfig.hooks = {
    onStart: (query, hookContext) => {
        console.log("Starting:", query);
    },
    onEnd: (query, durationMs, result, hookContext) => {
        console.log(`Completed in ${durationMs}ms:`, result);
    },
    onError: (query, error, result, hookContext) => {
        console.error("Failed:", error);
    }
};

docs.title: Custom transport
docs.text:
import { VConfig } from "@wxn0brp/vql-client";

VConfig.transport = async (query, fetchOptions) => {
    const res = await fetch("/custom-endpoint", {
        method: "POST",
        body: JSON.stringify({ query }),
        ...fetchOptions
    });
    return res.json();
};

docs.title: Browser global
docs.text:
When loaded with a script tag, the client is available as window.VQLClient:

VQLClient.cfg.url = "/api/vql";
const result = await VQLClient.fetchVQL("main users");
const item = await VQLClient.VQL`main items! s._id="123"`;

docs.title: VQLR (Object Syntax)
docs.text: VQLR is the object form of VQL. It is the internal representation produced by the VQLS parser and the preferred format for application code and generated queries.

docs.title: Query shapes
docs.text:
import type { VQL_Query, VQL_Query_CRUD, VQL_Query_Relation, VQL_Var } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/vql";

interface VQL_Query_CRUD {
    db: string;
    d: VQL_Query_CRUD_Data;
}

interface VQL_Query_Relation {
    r: {
        path: [string, string];
        search: Record<string, any>;
        relations: Record<string, RelationConfig>;
        many?: boolean;
        options?: DbFindOpts;
        select?: string[][] | Record<string, any>;
    };
}

type VQL_Query = (VQL_Query_CRUD | VQL_Query_Relation) & VQL_Var;

A query must contain db + d, or r. var is optional and is removed after variable expansion. If both shapes are present, r wins and the CRUD part is ignored.

docs.title: find
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_Find<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search?: Search<T>;
    limit?: number;
    select?: VQL_Fields;
    options?: DbFindOpts<T>;
    searchOpts?: FindOpts<T>;
}

{
    db: "main",
    d: {
        find: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { status: "active" },
            select: { name: 1, email: 1 },
            options: { limit: 10, sortBy: "name" },
            searchOpts: { exclude: ["internalNotes"] }
        }
    }
}

options is passed to the database as DbFindOpts. searchOpts is applied to the returned records and supports select, exclude, and transform.

A top-level select is merged into searchOpts.select and takes precedence. Use options.limit for limiting, not the top-level limit property. The limit field exists in the type for historical compatibility but the CRUD executor does not read it.

When combining select with sortBy, include the sort field in the selection. Selection is applied while records are processed, so selecting the field away can make the sort ineffective.

docs.title: findOne / f
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_FindOne<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search: Search<T>;
    select?: VQL_Fields;
    searchOpts?: FindOpts<T>;
}

{ db: "main", d: { findOne: { collection: "users", search: { _id: "123" } } } }
{ db: "main", d: { f: { collection: "users", search: { _id: "123" } } } }

search is required and must be an object. An empty object is valid.

docs.title: add
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_Add<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    data?: Arg<T>;
    id_gen?: boolean;
}

{ db: "main", d: { add: { collection: "users", data: { name: "Alice", age: 30 } } } }

id_gen defaults to true. When VQLConfig.allowEmptyAdd is true (the default), data may be omitted or empty. Set allowEmptyAdd: false to require a non-empty data object.

docs.title: update / updateOne
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_Update<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search: Search<T>;
    updater: UpdaterArg<T>;
    select?: VQL_Fields;
}

{
    db: "main",
    d: {
        update: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { role: "guest" },
            updater: { role: "user" },
            select: ["name"]
        }
    }
}

{
    db: "main",
    d: {
        updateOne: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { _id: "123" },
            updater: { name: "Bob", $inc: { loginCount: 1 } }
        }
    }
}

search and updater are required. Both update and updateOne operate on the matched records; updateOne affects at most one.

docs.title: remove / removeOne
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_Remove<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search: Search<T>;
    select?: VQL_Fields;
}

{ db: "main", d: { remove: { collection: "users", search: { active: false } } } }
{ db: "main", d: { removeOne: { collection: "users", search: { _id: "123" }, select: { name: 1 } } } }

Both operations return the removed records, filtered by select when provided.

docs.title: updateOneOrAdd
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_UpdateOneOrAdd<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search: Search<T>;
    updater: UpdaterArg<T>;
    add_arg?: Arg<T>;
    id_gen?: boolean;
    select?: VQL_Fields;
}

{
    db: "main",
    d: {
        updateOneOrAdd: {
            collection: "users",
            search: { _id: "123" },
            updater: { name: "Bob" },
            add_arg: { name: "Bob", email: "b@x.com" }
        }
    }
}

Returns { data, type }, where type is "added" or "updated". When add_arg is omitted, the insert payload is derived from the search and updater.

docs.title: toggleOne
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_ToggleOne<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search: Search<T>;
    data?: Arg<T>;
    select?: VQL_Fields;
}

{
    db: "main",
    d: {
        toggleOne: {
            collection: "favorites",
            search: { userId: "123", itemId: "456" },
            select: ["_id"]
        }
    }
}

Returns { data, type }, where type is "added" or "removed".

docs.title: count
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_Count<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    search?: Search<T>;
}

{ db: "main", d: { count: { collection: "users", search: { status: "active" } } } }

docs.title: bulkAdd
docs.text:
interface VQL_OP_BulkAdd<T = any> {
    collection: string;
    datas: Arg<T>[];
    id_gen?: boolean;
}

{ db: "main", d: { bulkAdd: { collection: "users", datas: [{ name: "Alice" }, { name: "Bob" }] } } }

docs.title: Collection management
docs.text:
{ db: "main", d: { ensureCollection: { collection: "logs" } } }
{ db: "main", d: { issetCollection: { collection: "logs" } } }
{ db: "main", d: { removeCollection: { collection: "temp" } } }
{ db: "main", d: { getCollections: {} } }

Collection operations return booleans, except getCollections, which returns string[].

docs.title: Relational queries
docs.text:
{
    r: {
        path: ["main", "orders"],
        search: { status: "pending" },
        many: true,
        relations: {
            customer: {
                path: ["main", "users"],
                pk: "customerId",
                fk: "_id",
                select: ["name", "email"]
            },
            items: {
                path: ["inventory", "products"],
                type: "1n",
                pk: "_id",
                fk: "orderId"
            }
        },
        select: [["_id"], ["customer", "name"], ["items"]]
    }
}

path, search, and relations are required. search and relations may be empty objects, but they must be present. many defaults to false, which performs a findOne. options accepts DbFindOpts.

select must be an array of segment arrays such as [["_id"], ["customer", "name"]]. Nested relation output uses the relation key: ["customer", "name"] selects the name field of the joined customer object. An object selector passes validation but is flattened to top-level keys and then fails at runtime, so use segment arrays for relations.

See Relations for all relation options.

docs.title: Field selection
docs.text:
select: { name: 1, email: 1 }
select: ["name", "email"]
select: ["profile.city", "settings.theme"]

Rules:

  • An omitted or empty selection means no filtering for CRUD. An empty relation selection also means no filtering without strictSelect, but selects no fields when strictSelect is true.
  • Arrays support dotted paths and ["a", "b"] segments for CRUD.
  • Records select fields with truthy values for CRUD; record selectors are not converted for relation queries.
  • Relation queries take segment arrays only. Dotted strings are not converted.
  • Permission checks add their own field-level filtering after execution.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
options (DbFindOpts):

Option Type Description reverse boolean Reverse the result order limit number Maximum number of records offset number Skip records sortBy string \| { field, asc }[] Sort field(s) sortAsc boolean Sort direction for sortBy min Record<string, string> Minimum aggregation per field max Record<string, string> Maximum aggregation per field avg Record<string, string> Average aggregation per field sum Record<string, string> Sum aggregation per field distinct string Distinct values of a field groupBy string \| string[] Group records count Record<string, string> Count aggregation

searchOpts (FindOpts):

Option Type Description select FieldPath[] Fields to keep exclude FieldPath[] Fields to remove transform Function Transform the record before other options

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Use { __: "name" } anywhere a value is expected. Strings starting with $ are also replaced by the variable value.

{
    db: "main",
    d: {
        add: {
            collection: "users",
            data: {
                ownerId: { __: "_me" },
                createdAt: { __: "_now" }
            }
        }
    },
    var: { role: "admin" }
}

Reserved names (_me, _user, _now, _nowShort, __now, __nowShort) cannot be overridden. See Language Overview.

docs.title: Response shapes
docs.text:
Operation Result find T[] findOne / f T \| null add T update T[] updateOne T \| null remove T[] removeOne T \| null updateOneOrAdd { data: T, type: "added" \| "updated" } toggleOne { data: T, type: "added" \| "removed" } count number bulkAdd T[] ensureCollection boolean issetCollection boolean removeCollection boolean getCollections string[]

VQLProcessor.execute() returns T | VQLError. Always check the result for errors.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
import VQLProcessor from "@wxn0brp/vql";
import type { VQLUQ } from "@wxn0brp/vql/types/vql";

const query: VQLUQ = {
    db: "main",
    d: {
        find: {
            collection: "users",
            search: {
                $and: [
                    { status: "active" },
                    { $gte: { age: 18 } }
                ]
            },
            options: { limit: 50, sortBy: [{ field: "age", asc: true }] },
            select: ["name", "email", "age", "profile.city"]
        }
    }
};

const result = await processor.execute(query);
if (result instanceof Error) {
    console.error(result.message);
} else {
    console.log(result);
}
