docs.title: VQLS (String Syntax)
docs.text: VQLS is a compact, line-oriented syntax for VQL. It is intended for CLI tools, configuration, logs, and places where embedding JSON is inconvenient.

docs.title: Grammar
docs.text:
<database> <operation> <collection> [body...]
<database> <collection-with-shorthand> [body...]

The body is a sequence of key=value tokens. Whitespace is flexible around =. A comparison operator such as > must follow the field name directly, without a space. Newlines are merged into one query, so a query may span several lines.

db users
s.status="active"
s.age>18
e.name=1

The same query on one line:

db users s.status="active" s.age>18 e.name=1

docs.title: Shorthands
docs.text:
Form Operation Example none find db users ! suffix findOne db users! + prefix add db +users ~ prefix update db ~users ~ prefix + ! suffix updateOne db ~users! - prefix remove db -users - prefix + ! suffix removeOne db -users! ? prefix updateOneOrAdd db ?users ^ prefix toggleOne db ^users # prefix count db #users * prefix bulkAdd db *users

A ! suffix on add is ignored, so db +users! is still an add.

docs.title: Explicit operations
docs.text:
db find users s.status="active"
db findOne users s._id="123"
db add users d.name="Alice"
db update users s.role="guest" u.role="user"
db updateOne users s._id="123" u.name="Bob"
db remove users s.active=false
db removeOne users s._id="123"
db updateOneOrAdd users s._id="123" u.name="Bob"
db toggleOne users s._id="123"
db count users s.status="active"
db bulkAdd users datas=[{"name":"Alice"},{"name":"Bob"}]
db ensureCollection logs
db issetCollection logs
db removeCollection temp_data
db getCollections

Use the explicit form when the collection name could be confused with an operation. Do not append ! to a collection passed to an explicit operation. The suffix is only parsed in shorthand form.

docs.title: Body aliases
Values
docs.text:
Type Syntax Example String "value", 'value', `value` s.name="Alice" Number Numeric literal s.age=25 Boolean true / false s.active=true JSON array [...] s.tags=["a","b"] JSON object {...} s={"$or":[{"a":1},{"b":2}]} Variable $name s.role=$role Anything else Unquoted string s.name=Alice

JSON values must be compact. Spaces, =, <, and > are treated as token separators even inside a {...} value, so s={"a": 1} is parsed incorrectly. Write s={"a":1} instead, or move the condition to a quoted string.

Quoted strings may contain spaces, =, <, and >. A backslash escapes the next character, for example "He said \"hi\"".

Numbers are parsed as numbers. Quote identifiers to keep them as strings:

db users s.externalId="12345"

null cannot be written as a bare literal because it is parsed as the string "null". Use a JSON object for the whole search object when you need null:

db users s={"deletedAt":null}

An empty value at the end of a query becomes true:

db users s.active=

Prefer the explicit form (s.active=true) to avoid ambiguity when more tokens follow.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Comparison operators are written between the field and the value:

Syntax VQLR equivalent s.age=25 { age: 25 } s.age>18 { $gt: { age: 18 } } s.age>=18 { $gte: { age: 18 } } s.age<65 { $lt: { age: 65 } } s.age<=65 { $lte: { age: 65 } }

Other operators use their $ name directly as part of the key:

db users s.$ne.status="deleted"
db users s.$in.role=["admin","mod"]
db users s.$between.age=[18,65]
db users s.$exists.email=true
db users s.$startsWith.name="Al"
db users s.$arrInc.tags=["new"]

For complex logical conditions, either use numeric path segments or assign a JSON object:

db users s.$or.0.role="admin" s.$or.1.ownerId=$_me
db users s={"$and":[{"status":"active"},{"age":{"$gt":18}}]}

Regular expressions cannot be expressed as RegExp instances in VQLS. Raw pattern strings are accepted by ValtheraDB but deprecated, so prefer VQLR when you need /pattern/ semantics.

Updater operators use the same $ notation:

db ~users s._id="123" u.$inc.loginCount=1 u.$set.lastSeen=$_now

docs.title: Field selection
docs.text:
db users s.status="active" e.name=1 e.email=1

For CRUD operations, VQLS converts e. keys into a top-level field list: e.profile.city=1 selects the whole profile object. Use VQLR if you need a nested selection path for CRUD.

Relation queries keep nested paths, but only when the query runs in relation mode. Add an r. key:

db orders e._id=1 e.customer.name=1
r.customer.path=["main","users"]
many=true

Without r., e.orders.total=1 is a CRUD query and the select collapses to the top-level orders field.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
o. maps to database find options:

db users o.limit=10 o.offset=20 o.sortBy=name o.sortAsc=false

Use o.limit, not a top-level limit property. See VQLR for the full option list.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
A query becomes a relation query when the body contains an r. key.

db users s.status="active" e.name=1 e.orders.total=1
r.orders.path=["shop","orders"]
r.orders.select=["total","status"]
many=true

Per-relation search (for example r.orders.search.status="pending") is accepted by the validator but is not applied when the relation is loaded. Filter the parent query with s. or r.search instead, or query the related collection separately.

Each relation entry is keyed by the output field name. path is [database, collection]. When path is omitted, it defaults to [current-db, relation-name]. The db and c keys are shorthand for the same values:

db users r.orders.db="shop" r.orders.c="orders"

Nested relations use the same dotted structure:

db users r.orders.path=["shop","orders"] r.orders.relations.items.path=["shop","items"]

r.x.select must be a JSON array. A dotted object such as r.orders.select.name=1 fails validation because relation selects are arrays.

Top-level relation options do not use the r. prefix:

many=true
options.limit=10

r. always creates a relation entry, so r.many=true would define a relation named many instead of setting the root option.

See Relations for pk, fk, type, through, and nested select semantics.

docs.title: Collection operations
docs.text:
db ensureCollection logs
db issetCollection logs
db removeCollection logs
db getCollections

getCollections is a special two-token query and takes no collection argument.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Lines whose first non-space characters are # or // are ignored. Trailing comments on the same line are not supported.

# Active users
db users s.status="active"
// Only the first page
o.limit=10

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Find with filter and selection
db users s.status="active" s.age>18 e.name=1 e.email=1 o.limit=10

# Add a record
db +users d.name="Alice" d.email="alice@example.com" d.age=30

# Update one record and return selected fields
db ~users! s._id="123" u.name="Bob" u.updatedAt=$_now e.name=1 e.updatedAt=1

# Update many records
db ~users s.role="guest" u.role="user" e._id=1 e.name=1

# Upsert
db ?users s._id="123" u.name="Bob" u.lastSeen=$_now e.name=1

# Delete with selected return fields
db -users s.active=false e._id=1 e.name=1
db -users! s._id="123" e.name=1

# Toggle
db ^users s._id="123" e._id=1

# Count
db #users s.status="active"

# Bulk insert
db *users datas=[{"name":"Alice"},{"name":"Bob"}]

# Relation query
db users s.status="active"
r.orders.path=["shop","orders"]
r.orders.select=["total","status"]
many=true
e.name=1 e.orders.total=1

# Collection management
db ensureCollection logs
db getCollections

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Explicit operations do not strip the ! suffix from the collection name.
  • Bare null, undefined, and functions are not supported. Use JSON for null.
  • Duplicate keys overwrite earlier values.
  • A comparison operator always applies to the whole dotted path after the alias: s.a.b>1 becomes { $gt: { a: { b: 1 } } }.
  • An empty value consumes the next token as its value. Keep key= at the end of the body or use an explicit value.
  • e. collapses nested paths for CRUD operations. Use VQLR for nested CRUD selects.
  • r.x.search is validated but ignored by the relation loader. Use s. or r.search on the parent query.
  • JSON values must be compact: s={"a":1} works, s={"a": 1} does not.
  • With an explicit operation and no body, a dotted collection name is misparsed: db find my.col treats find as the collection. Add a body token or use the shorthand db my.col.
  • The parser has no implicit type conversion beyond numbers, booleans, and JSON.
  • r.many=true is parsed as a relation named many. Use many=true for the root relation option.

docs.title: Language Overview
docs.text:
VQL provides two interchangeable query syntaxes that compile to the same internal representation and execute through the same code path.

Syntax Format Best for VQLS String CLI tools, config files, quick scripts, logs VQLR Object Application code, TypeScript, generated queries

Both syntaxes accept the universal query wrapper:

type VQLUQ<T = any> =
    | VQL_Query<T>
    | string
    | { query: string; var?: Record<string, any> };

VQLProcessor.execute() accepts any of these forms, plus a user context used by variables and permissions.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Operation VQLS shorthand VQLR key Returns find db collection find T[] findOne db collection! findOne or f T \| null add db +collection add T update db ~collection update T[] updateOne db ~collection! updateOne T \| null remove db -collection remove T[] removeOne db -collection! removeOne T \| null updateOneOrAdd db ?collection updateOneOrAdd { data: T, type: "added" \| "updated" } toggleOne db ^collection toggleOne { data: T, type: "added" \| "removed" } count db #collection count number bulkAdd db *collection bulkAdd T[] ensureCollection db ensureCollection name ensureCollection boolean issetCollection db issetCollection name issetCollection boolean removeCollection db removeCollection name removeCollection boolean getCollections db getCollections getCollections string[]

docs.title: Body prefixes
docs.text:
VQLS uses short prefixes for the body. VQLR uses the full property names.

Prefix VQLR property Purpose s. search Search/filter conditions d. data Data payload for add and toggleOne u. updater Update payload o. options Database find options (limit, sort, offset) r. relations Relation query, switches to relation mode e. select Field selection

For update and remove, a d. payload is automatically treated as u. when no u. value is present.

docs.title: Search operators
docs.text:
VQL passes search objects to ValtheraDB. Everything below is supported in VQLR. In VQLS, comparison operators have shorthand syntax and all other operators are written with their $ name (see VQLS).

Operator Meaning Example equality Field equals value { status: "active" } $ne Not equal { $ne: { status: "deleted" } } $gt Greater than { $gt: { age: 18 } } $lt Less than { $lt: { price: 100 } } $gte Greater or equal { $gte: { age: 18 } } $lte Less or equal { $lte: { price: 100 } } $between Inclusive range { $between: { age: [18, 65] } } $in Value in array { $in: { role: ["admin", "mod"] } } $nin Value not in array { $nin: { status: ["banned"] } } $exists Field presence { $exists: { email: true } } $type JavaScript type name { $type: { age: "number" } } $and All conditions match { $and: [{ status: "a" }, { age: { $gt: 18 } }] } $or Any condition matches { $or: [{ role: "admin" }, { ownerId: "u1" }] } $not Negate a condition { $not: { status: "deleted" } } $regex Regular expression { $regex: { name: /^A/i } } $startsWith String prefix { $startsWith: { name: "Al" } } $endsWith String suffix { $endsWith: { email: "@x.com" } } $iStartsWith Case-insensitive prefix { $iStartsWith: { name: "al" } } $iEndsWith Case-insensitive suffix { $iEndsWith: { email: "@X.COM" } } $arrInc Array includes value { $arrInc: { tags: ["new"] } } $arrIncAll Array includes all values { $arrIncAll: { tags: ["a", "b"] } } $size Array length { $size: { tags: 3 } } $subset Literal $ keys in data { $subset: { "$ref": "x" } }

Nested fields can be targeted by nesting the operator:

{ $gt: { profile: { age: 18 } } }

Plain nested objects are also valid equality conditions:

{ profile: { city: "NYC" } }

docs.title: Updater operators
Field selection
docs.text:
select accepts either an array of field paths or a record of field flags.

select: { name: 1, email: 1, internal: 0 }
select: ["name", "email", "profile.city"]

Rules:

  • An omitted or empty selection means "no selection", so the full record is returned.
  • Arrays support dotted paths such as profile.city.
  • Records keep fields whose value is truthy.
  • For CRUD operations in VQLS, e. paths are collapsed to their top-level field. Use VQLR when you need a nested path for CRUD.
  • Relation queries keep nested paths only as segment arrays such as [["profile", "city"]]. Dotted strings and record selectors are not converted for relations.
  • For array relations (1n, nm), select the relation key as a whole. Field picking does not traverse arrays.
  • With permissions enabled, returned objects are filtered per field. See Permissions.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variables are resolved after the top-level shape check and before the detailed validation and execution.

docs.title: Predefined variables
docs.text:
Variable Value _me user.id \|\| user._id \|\| user _user Full user object _now Date.now() in milliseconds _nowShort Date.now() / 1000 rounded down __now Date.now().toString() __nowShort Seconds as a string

Predefined names cannot be overridden by the var object.

docs.title: Custom variables
docs.text:
In VQLS, a value starting with $ references a variable:

db users s.role=$role u.lastSeen=$_now

In VQLR, use the reference object:

{
    db: "main",
    d: { add: { collection: "users", data: { ownerId: { __: "_me" }, createdAt: { __: "_now" } } } },
    var: { role: "admin" }
}

Pass variables alongside a string query:

await processor.execute({
    query: "main users s.role=$role",
    var: { role: "admin" }
});

Unresolved variables are left untouched. Objects that contain __ but do not match a known variable also stay unchanged.
